definition: The league's own id for this registration
rationale: Lets a correction or a deletion request point at one row. Not a person id: the platform makes that.

definition: Canonical id of the league from the issued league registry
rationale: Replaces the free-text league name and the vendor's own codes: removes the largest source of unattributable records.
Needed to count a child once per season and to measure timeliness.
Two seasons a year in the US; a child can legitimately play both, so the term is part of the counting key.
Mixed-sport associations must send flag registrations only: tackle players are out of purpose, so their data is not requested.

retention_rule: Deleted at age-out plus grace (configurable; the period is an open question)
rationale: Needed to tell that two registrations are one child. The only direct identifier of the child; never leaves the restricted zone, never reaches a club.
Enough for age band and for matching (see the minimization experiment in this document). Full date of birth is deliberately not requested.

format: M, F, X or U (not disclosed)
rationale: Girls' participation is a headline measure. U is a valid answer: a parent can decline, and a decline is not a defect.

definition: First three digits of the home ZIP
rationale: Placing a child in a club market needs only the ZIP3 (the market map is built on ZIP3). The last two digits are not requested.

retention_rule: Deleted at age-out plus grace, or at once on consent revocation
rationale: The household key and the only contact route. Collected for league operations and consent; using it for marketing needs its own opt-in (purpose limitation).
Timeliness is a quality dimension; without a timestamp it cannot be measured.

retention_rule: As long as the consent is relied on, then deleted with the household
rationale: Provenance: when. Required for any household that club activation will include; optional otherwise.

definition: Version or hash of the consent wording shown
rationale: Provenance: on which wording. Without it nobody can say what the parent agreed to.

format: LEAGUE_OPERATIONS, LEAGUE_COMMUNICATIONS, NFL_CLUB_MARKETING, THIRD_PARTY_DISCLOSURE, PROFILING, joined by |
rationale: Provenance: what. A parental-consent email is not a marketing opt-in; only NFL_CLUB_MARKETING makes a household eligible for club activation.
Provenance: how. A paper slip and a checkbox carry different evidence.
